source_evidence.anchor: Exercise 2.3.2, complete statement and displayed inequality
source_evidence.observation: The exercise asks the reader to modify the proof of Theorem 2.3.1 and states: for any t < mu, P{S_N <= t} <= exp(-mu)(e mu/t)^t.
The inherited setting consists of independent Bernoulli random variables X_i with parameters p_i, their sum S_N = sum_{i=1}^N X_i, and its mean mu = E[S_N].

source_evidence.anchor: Proof of Theorem 2.3.1, Bernoulli MGF paragraph and product bound
source_evidence.observation: The source describes X_i as 1 with probability p_i and 0 with probability 1-p_i, and identifies mu with sum_i p_i in the MGF calculation.

source_evidence.anchor: Exercise 2.3.2 phrase 'lower tail' and event in its display
source_evidence.observation: The target event is the inclusive lower-tail event S_N <= t.

The later source applies Exercise 2.3.2 at t = (1-delta)mu, including the endpoint delta = 1 in its stated range, which makes the substituted threshold zero and exposes a boundary case not covered by a positive-threshold reading of the displayed formula.

binders: A finite family X_1, ..., X_N of random variables and Bernoulli parameters p_1, ..., p_N, inherited from Theorem 2.3.1 (PDF page 7, printed page 18, theorem opening sentence).
A real threshold t, printed as universally quantified subject only to t < mu (PDF page 8, printed page 19, Exercise 2.3.2).
hypotheses: The X_i are mutually independent Bernoulli random variables with respective parameters p_i (PDF page 7, printed page 18, Theorem 2.3.1).
S_N is their sum and mu is E[S_N] (PDF page 7, printed page 18, Theorem 2.3.1).
The printed threshold condition is t < mu, with no explicit assumption t > 0 (PDF page 8, printed page 19, Exercise 2.3.2).
conclusions: The source displays P{S_N <= t} <= exp(-mu)(e mu/t)^t (PDF page 8, printed page 19, Exercise 2.3.2).
definitions_and_conventions: S_N := sum_{i=1}^N X_i and mu := E[S_N] (PDF page 7, printed page 18, Theorem 2.3.1).
For these Bernoulli variables, X_i equals 1 with probability p_i and 0 with probability 1-p_i, and mu = sum_i p_i (PDF page 8, printed page 19, proof of Theorem 2.3.1).

The displayed power (e mu/t)^t has its usual real-analytic Chernoff meaning for a positive base; the source does not provide a convention extending it through t = 0 or negative base values (PDF page 8, printed page 19, Exercise 2.3.2 display).
implicit_context: All probabilities and expectations use the ambient probability space carrying the independent variables (PDF pages 7-8, printed pages 18-19, Theorem 2.3.1 and its proof).
The family need not be identically distributed because the source assigns individual parameters p_i (PDF page 7, printed page 18, Theorem 2.3.1).
Because each Bernoulli variable is nonnegative, S_N and mu are nonnegative (PDF page 8, printed page 19, the explicit 0/1 description of X_i and mu = sum_i p_i).
The title and prose identify the claim as a lower-tail analogue of Theorem 2.3.1 (PDF page 8, printed page 19, Exercise 2.3.2).

details: The event is one-sided and inclusive: S_N <= t (PDF page 8, printed page 19, displayed inequality).
The threshold is below the mean according to the printed condition t < mu (same statement).
The upper bound is exactly exp(-mu)(e mu/t)^t, matching the algebraic form of Theorem 2.3.1 but in the lower-tail regime (PDF pages 7-8, printed pages 18-19).
The printed source says only t < mu, although the quotient mu/t and real power require special treatment at t <= 0 (PDF page 8, printed page 19, Exercise 2.3.2).
The mathematically standard nondegenerate domain for the displayed expression is 0 < t < mu; this is an analyst diagnosis of the printed domain issue, not an additional source hypothesis.
The inherited setting permits mu = 0 because endpoint Bernoulli parameters are not excluded (PDF pages 7-8, printed pages 18-19).

At t = 0 the displayed right-hand side divides by zero, and for negative t with positive mu its base e mu/t is negative and does not have a general real power (PDF page 8, printed page 19, displayed formula).
The instruction is to modify Theorem 2.3.1's MGF proof rather than invoke a separately named theorem (PDF page 8, printed page 19, first sentence of Exercise 2.3.2).

undebatable_constraints: The variables are independent Bernoulli variables with individual parameters p_i (PDF page 7, printed page 18, Theorem 2.3.1).
S_N is their finite sum and mu is E[S_N] = sum_i p_i (PDF pages 7-8, printed pages 18-19).
The source prints the threshold condition t < mu and does not print 0 < t (PDF page 8, printed page 19, Exercise 2.3.2).
The event is the inclusive lower-tail event S_N <= t (PDF page 8, printed page 19, displayed inequality).
The displayed right-hand side is exp(-mu)(e mu/t)^t (PDF page 8, printed page 19, displayed inequality).

ambiguities.issue: The printed domain omits the positivity condition needed for the displayed quotient and general real power.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 8, printed page 19 says 'For any t < mu' and then displays exp(-mu)(e mu/t)^t; it gives no convention for t = 0 or negative bases.
ambiguities.impact: Taken literally over all real t < mu, the right-hand side is undefined at t = 0 and generally undefined for negative t. The standard meaningful correction is 0 < t < mu, but a formalization adopting that restriction is correcting or narrowing the printed statement and must record the discrepancy.

ambiguities.issue: The source does not explicitly exclude the degenerate mean mu = 0.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 2.3.1 allows Bernoulli parameters without strict positivity, and its proof gives mu = sum_i p_i (PDF pages 7-8, printed pages 18-19).
ambiguities.impact: If mu = 0 there is no t satisfying the standard repaired domain 0 < t < mu, whereas the literal printed domain admits negative t for which the displayed expression lacks a real-valued meaning.

ambiguities.issue: The subsequent endpoint use t = (1-delta)mu at delta = 1 is not directly covered by the standard positive-threshold repair.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 9, printed page 20 states delta in (0,1] and tells the reader to apply Exercise 2.3.2 at t = (1-delta)mu.
ambiguities.impact: The zero-threshold lower-tail case must be handled separately or obtained by a limiting argument; it cannot be justified by direct substitution into the displayed quotient.

contract_plain_english: In the setting of Theorem 2.3.1, with independent Bernoulli variables X_i, sum S_N, and mean mu, the source intends a Chernoff upper bound for the lower-tail probability P{S_N <= t}: exp(-mu)(e mu/t)^t. The book prints only t < mu. Because the displayed expression divides by t and raises its base to a real exponent, the formula is mathematically well-defined in its standard form for 0 < t < mu; the missing positivity condition is a genuine source-domain issue and must not be silently erased.
